channel.title: Caleb Hart · Blog
channel.description: Caleb Hart is a data scientist and data engineer who builds AI, machine learning, RAG and business intelligence solutions in Python, SQL and Power BI, and teaches people how to use AI well.

item.title: A month of letting three AI agents run a research desk
item.description: From October 11 to November 7, three Claude agents researched, fact-checked and published 68 posts on frontier AI. What worked, what broke, and what I'd change.

item.title: Turning my old mining rig into a local LLM server
item.description: How I'm turning a retired four-GPU mining rig into a fully local, Claude Code style coding agent: the hardware, the software map, and why each piece is there.

item.title: The LLM demo that paid dividends
item.description: I blanked on what RAG stood for in a job interview, so a week later I showed up with one: a local chatbot over the company's 247 web pages and 73 PDFs. Here's the story and every line of the code.

item.title: My time at Poudre Valley REA
item.description: AI and BI at an electric co-op: data governance, source control for hundreds of analytics assets, automation, RAG systems and AI training for 60 people.

item.title: My thoughts on Brené Brown's Dare to Lead
item.description: Overall, Dare to Lead is a great read on leadership skills and deconstructing false beliefs about vulnerability, shame, courage, and how your values make you a better leader.

item.title: Two skies, one giraffe: a code walkthrough of my pixel-art portrait
item.description: How a 48×48 numpy array becomes the sunset giraffe in dark mode and the sunrise giraffe in light mode, walked through line by line.

item.title: Manager or facilitator? What a LinkedIn course taught me about leading
item.description: I recently completed LinkedIn's course "Facilitation Skills for Managers and Leaders".

item.title: MIT's report on AI and education, and why it matters beyond the classroom
item.description: I recently read MIT's new report on AI and Education, and it made me happy to see a strong stance being taken in education.

item.title: Foundation Model Spotlight: why Chronos-2 is still everywhere
item.description: Why is Chronos-2 still being used heavily to create new foundation models?

item.title: My time as an applied data scientist and professional poker player
item.description: Nine months playing poker professionally and building a reinforcement-learning lab for it: 10 million simulated games, CFR versus Deep CFR, PPO and an XGBoost returns forecast.

item.title: My time at Hart2Chart
item.description: Running my own web development and consulting practice: one-week delivery cycles, portfolios and dashboards for clients, a 5-star rating, and the framework that became AtlasHTMLCharts.

item.title: My time at the Oregon Tech Peer Tutoring Center
item.description: Three and a half years as a public speaking tutor: speech coaching, drafting and speaking anxiety, for up to four classes a semester.

item.title: Store sales forecasting with gradient boosting, delivered to your inbox
item.description: XGBoost on high-dimensional retail data, LightGBM comparisons on a live dashboard, and automated forecast emails that saved 10 hours a week.

item.title: Teaching an agent to play Minesweeper
item.description: A custom Gymnasium environment, REINFORCE versus DQN and SARSA, and what about 900 training episodes taught me about exploration.

item.title: Forecasting a year of USDA meat and poultry production
item.description: A VAE and a transformer on decades of seasonal USDA production data, with automated pipelines, outlier detection and an honest look at the results.

item.title: What 2 million RuneScape hiscores say about players
item.description: Can boss kill counts predict a player's total XP? Random forests, sparse data, K-means clustering and an R² of 0.76 on Old School RuneScape hiscores.

item.title: Designing a trading card price scanner
item.description: A system analysis and design project for a phone app that recognizes a trading card from a photo and looks up its market price.

item.title: A writing tracker in R Shiny: 151,170 words in six months
item.description: The R Shiny dashboard I built to track my daily writing across personal writing, outlines and my novel, with radar charts and monthly goals.

item.title: Fine-tuning T5 to comment Python code
item.description: A four-person team project: picking from six NLP ideas, switching from CodeBERT to T5 mid-project, and a tkinter app that writes docstrings.

item.title: Bringing solar light to 24 homes in rural Kenya
item.description: Co-leading a solar installation from start to finish, and teaching programming and robotics to high school classes in rural Kenya.

item.title: My time at Windsor FTC Robotics
item.description: Six months as an associate engineer and teacher with STEM Education Inc., teaching robotics in rural Kenya and co-leading a solar install.
